statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail stays low because CME equity index futures have been shut since Friday 21:00Z and no live NQ price path exists, while Stress edges further into the high band on a 5.18% 10-year yield at its highest since 2007, WTI at $92.41 and Brent at $104.32 with the Strait of Hormuz still closed, a rejected Iranian reopening roadmap, and Sunday remarks from a senior Iranian commander that the waterway stays shut until US economic pressure ends.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. A narrow danger window is published from the 22:00Z CME equity index futures restart into the early Asian hours, where the withdrawn diplomatic premise behind part of Friday's oil decline would first be expressed in price. Existing-position management and emergency protection logic are unaffected by this publication.
headline: Nasdaq-100 Tail stays low with futures shut, while a hardening Hormuz stance, record AI-linked bond supply and a 5.18% 10-year yield hold Stress high into the 22:00Z restart
body:
Equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00Z, so there is no live NQ price path at this assessment time and the current Tail reading reflects an absent path rather than an observed benign trend. Friday's verified cash close was orderly: the Nasdaq-100 finished at 30,608.14, up 0.42% from a 30,478.90 prior close, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 day range, while VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 after a 15.94 session high. Contemporaneous reporting has the S&P 500 up 0.51% at 7,743.41, the Nasdaq Composite up 0.48% at 27,068.72 and the Dow up 0.93% at 51,828.62. That combination shows no shallow-pullback extension, no holding of session extremes and no volatility stress, so the amplifiers this contract requires before Tail reaches the elevated band are absent.

Stress rises one point to 69 on two inputs that firmed since the last publication. The geopolitical track hardened rather than stalled: after Washington publicly rejected Tehran's seven-day roadmap on Saturday, a plan that required lifting the naval blockade, waiving oil sanctions and releasing frozen funds, a senior Iranian commander said on Sunday that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until US economic pressure ends. Iran separately claimed to have seized an advanced American underwater vehicle in the strait, a claim the US military disputed while stating it retains positive control of its drone assets. Tehran still says it awaits a definitive reply through mediators, so the diplomatic track is stalled rather than terminated and headline risk into the restart is two-sided. The second input is rates and AI credit. H.15 puts the 10-year at 5.18%, the 2-year at 4.87% and the 30-year at 5.47%, with the 10-year at its highest level since 2007. Reporting published Sunday puts global AI-linked bond issuance above $400bn in 2026, an annualised pace beyond $500bn with roughly 90% from US issuers, against projected capital spending near $800bn this year and about $1.2tn next year across five large platforms; the Federal Reserve chair is quoted saying competition for capital is real and partly explains the increase in yields. Energy remains the third standing input, with WTI settled at $92.41, down 2.33%, and Brent at $104.32, down 2.14%, specifically on the reopening optimism that has now been withdrawn.

The important distinction is that none of this is yet a price path. Under this contract event importance, diplomatic reversal and surprise magnitude inform Stress and Confidence until observed market structure supports Tail, so the mapped state stays EA_ON and the protection is expressed as a narrow danger window across the 22:00Z restart rather than a broad shutdown. Cross-asset internals still argue against alignment: on the latest session 6 of 8 megacaps rose but dispersion was 1.92%, with MSFT up 3.66% against META down 3.33%, and 6 of 7 semiconductors rose with QCOM up 3.97% against INTC down 3.45%, while Technology added 0.85% against Communication Services down 0.58%. That is rotation, not the uniform one-way alignment that would amplify Tail. The week ahead supplies the catalysts that are currently absent: JOLTS openings and CB consumer confidence on Tuesday, PCE and core PCE with ADP and final Q2 GDP on Wednesday, ISM manufacturing on Thursday and September non-farm payrolls on Friday.

Confidence improves to 78. Verified index, volatility, yield, crude and seven-day calendar evidence is complete, and the weekend and Sunday geopolitical developments were each corroborated across multiple independent outlets. Offsetting that, there is still no live price path during the futures halt, several primary outlets returned bot-block responses and were verified indirectly, and the shared Finviz context was 186 minutes old at this assessment with collection status partial and its futures and calendar sections unavailable. That context is therefore treated as stale under the 90-minute freshness rule and its breadth, megacap and semiconductor readings were used only as labelled latest-session, non-real-time confirmation evidence.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots are available from published Claude assessments and were carried forward unchanged. Tail held in a narrow 6-8 band, Stress rose from 52 to 68, and Confidence decayed from 80 to a 67 trough around 08:00Z before recovering to 77 as weekend evidence was verified. The mapped state remained EA_ON with dominant mode normal throughout, reflecting an orderly Friday cash session followed by a weekend with no live price discovery and an increasingly demanding rates, energy and geopolitical backdrop.
outlookSummary: The forecast keeps Tail in the low band across all 24 hours, so the mapped state stays EA_ON throughout. Risk holds near the closed-period baseline through the remainder of Sunday, then lifts from roughly 19:00Z into the published danger window at the 22:00Z CME equity index futures restart, where the rejected Hormuz roadmap and a hardening Iranian stance meet the thinnest liquidity of the week. Conditional Tail peaks at 16 in the restart hour, then decays through the Asian session as depth improves, easing to single digits before the European open. A modest lift to 11 is carried across the 13:30Z US cash open and to 12 across the first full cash hour containing the 14:30Z Dallas Fed manufacturing survey, where opening-auction continuation without a shallow pullback would be the first genuine Tail evidence of the week. Every forecast hour beyond the current one is conditional risk, not an assertion that future price structure has been observed.
